newsitem.title: UK: Delta's new chief plans for expansion.
newsitem.headline: Delta's new chief plans for expansion.

text.p: Electrical cables to industrial services and engineering group Delta Plc announced a fall in annual profits on Tuesday but its new chief executive promised a shakeup in strategy.
Jon Scott-Maxwell, who took up his appointment in December, said a new plan for growth was now being drawn up.

"Those businesses and markets with the best potential for long term profitable growth are being analysed to determine what is required to enable Delta to realise the potential they offer," he said in the results statement.

"This process...will enable the group to decide how best to realise the full potential of its strengths, where the main focus should be, what geographical cover is desirable and how best to exploit or modify the traditionally vertically integrated operations."
Earlier the company reported that annual pretax profits fell to 45.6 million pounds last year from 53.1 million in 1995.

Underlying profits slipped 1.2 million pounds to 62.9 million pounds. A slump in copper prices last year dented the results with a 5.7 million pound writedown on stocks, and rationalisation work and disposals took a further toll with exceptional charges of 11.6 million pounds.

Earnings after exceptionals fell to 15.2 pence a share from 20p in 1995. But Delta said underlying earnings would have been 25.2p but for the copper price factor and exceptionals against 26.1p in 1995. The dividend payout was maintained at 18.9 pence a share.

It said demand in European markets was subdued but it won an "encouraging" number of orders from new markets last year and the benefits of rationalisation were starting to come through in its cables division.
But the company said the end of the year "saw some signs of strengthening demand in the UK and some recovery in the price of copper".
